newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Violent Pakistan quake kills at least eight people.
newsitem.headline: Violent Pakistan quake kills at least eight people.

text.p: A severe earthquake hit southwestern Pakistan early on Friday, killing at least eight people and injuring many others in Baluchistan province bordering Iran and Afghanistan, residents and officials said.

A government seismic centre in the northwestern town of Peshawar measured the earthquake at 6.0 on the Richter scale. It placed the epicentre in the Koh-i-Suleman mountain range, north of the Baluchistan province capital Quetta, near the Afghan border, it said.
The U.S. Geological Survey's National Earthquake Information Centre in Golden, Colorado, measured the quake at 7.3 on the Richter scale.

Frank Baldwin, a physical science technician at the centre, said the quake occurred at 2108 GMT and was centred 70 miles (110 km) east southeast of Quetta, or 395 miles (630 km) southwest of Islamabad.
It was followed 22 minutes later by an aftershock measuring 6.3 on the Richter scale, he said.
At least three people were killed and 20 injured in Quetta and five were killed in Sibi to the southeast, doctors said.
Several other districts in the province were also jolted, but there was no immediate reports of casualties.

Earlier, an official at the Pakistan seismic centre had described the quake as violent and said its strength could be The quake struck Quetta at 2.10 a.m. (2110 GMT Thursday). Another jolt came 20 minutes later and mild tremors continued even two hours after the first quake.
Many people left their homes despite the freezing cold and even hospital patients fled their wards with their beds, residents said.
Others, including hotel occupants, were seen on streets sheltering from the cold with quilts and blankets.
"First there was a mild tremor, then it became very severe and it sounded as though a tractor was running outside," one resident said.
Islamic religious men went to mosques and called Azan, the Moslem call for prayers, as is usually done in the event of calamity. Others fired automatic weapons in the air to wake up people.
The region is prone to earthquakes. Quetta was destroyed by an earthquake on May 31, 1935 that measured 7.5 on the Richter scale and killed 30,000 people.
Hours after the first jolt, local authorities made announcements through loudspeakers warning residents against staying indoors and telling them there was danger of more tremors.
